name: Cendre Green
lede: Cendre Green is a light yellowish green from Ridgway's 1912 plates, and the exact same swatch our library also files, under a different name, as Mint Leaf.

sections.title: One swatch, two names
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature plates it at plate VI, hue 35, tone b, hex #7DC18B [1]. The ISCC-NBS committee's 1955 match places it in block 130 among the "brilliant yellowish green" names, 3.8 units away [1]. The library carries an identical hex, rgb and Munsell notation, 1.7G 7.2/6.3, under a second name, [[mint-leaf|Mint Leaf]], which the ISCC-NBS committee separately filed in block 132, a plant-derived name rather than a dictionary one [1]. Two names, two ISCC-NBS blocks, one exact color: the dictionaries did not always agree on which named swatch belonged to which category [1].

Its other nearby library names are [[neuwieder-green|Neuwieder Green]] and [[arcadian-green|Arcadian Green]], both about three units away [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within six units of Cendre Green covers at least five per cent of the canvas in only 5 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. Its earliest and largest appearance is a 1795 *Portrait of Emperor Jahangir*, where it covers 51 per cent of the canvas [2]. It also turns up twice in Vincent van Gogh's paintings, *Roulin's Baby* (1888) and a still life of oranges and lemons (1889) [2]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, read as screen colors; five matches is too few to draw a pattern from [2].

disambiguation.gloss: Mint Leaf is the exact same hex, filed under a different ISCC-NBS block (132, a plant-derived name) instead of Cendre Green's block 130
